item.title: CAPITAL IDEAS: What if oil hits $150? - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: If the market comes to believe $150 oil is not a spike but a plateau (at least a temporary one), I expect the S&P 500 to trade less like a traditional geopolitical scare and more like a classic recession scare.

item.title: BUSINESS MONDAY: Spotlight on Sarah's Cheesecakes & Cafe in Pittsfield - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The small family-owned and -operated operation is celebrating its 20th anniversary—and looking forward to many more years to come.

item.title: PETER MOST: A strategy to fix the regional school funding formula - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: While State Rep. Leigh Davis is working on behalf of Great Barrington in this legislative session, the next question is: What can the town do on a parallel track?

item.title: BUSINESS PERSPECTIVES: Berkshire Boulders rock-climbing gym to open in Great Barrington this summer - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: "When I look at the Berkshires at large, I see a ton of potential," said Berkshire Boulders co-owner Nick Friedman. "There are certain forms of outdoor recreation in the Berkshires that remain underrepresented, and there's a real opportunity on the table to bring better representation to these sports."

item.title: The Lee Public Safety Complex: Take a hard hat tour of the site but without the hard hat - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Progress continues on the new build set for a 2027 opening.

item.title: World Tuberculosis Day is March 24 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: We can identify, treat, and cure tuberculosis. So why is it still so prevalent? This disease preys upon the marginalized, undernourished, and immunocompromised.

item.title: In response to William Perry's 'Some Thoughts About Spring,' some songs from the Great American Songbook about spring - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Instead of celebrating spring, "Spring is Here" and "Spring Can Really Hang You Up The Most" bemoan the coming of spring.

item.title: Why are Arthur Batacchi and Kimberly Alcantara still on the Southern Berkshire Regional School Committee? - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The time has come to get some new people on the School Committee.

item.title: FILM REVIEW: Huo Meng's 'Living the Land' opens at the Film Forum on April 3 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The film, which is a bit too leisurely, is less focused on individual character than on community and extended family—forces that, alongside a distant and repressive government, define their lives.
